name: Colmar
tagline: Half-timbered canals and the Alsace wine route
summary: Colmar is a storybook Alsace town of painted half-timbered houses and flower-lined canals. Drift through Little Venice by boat, see the Isenheim Altarpiece in the Unterlinden Museum, then follow the wine route to Riquewihr and Eguisheim, and come in December for some of France's best Christmas markets.
seasonNote: Late spring and the September harvest are lovely; Christmas markets run late November to late December and are crowded.
arrival: TGV trains from Paris take 2h20; Basel-Mulhouse airport is 45 minutes away.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; buses or a car (or bike) for the wine villages.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; Christmas market stalls may want cash.
foodTip: Choucroute garnie, tarte flambée (flammekueche), baeckeoffe stew and kougelhopf cake, with Riesling and Gewürztraminer.
buyTip: Alsace wines, gingerbread and Munster cheese.
